issues.description: The helper method singFarmSongVerse has a parameter mismatch: the problem UML shows singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void and the solution implements singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal), but the template method declaration currently has no formal parameter (the Animal parameter is commented out). This inconsistency between template and solution/problem statement can confuse students about the intended signature and may lead to incorrect implementations or compilation errors if tests expect the Animal parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Farm.java to declare singFarmSongVerse with the Animal parameter (e.g., private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }) to match the problem UML and the solution. This clarifies the intended signature for students. Alternatively, if a different signature is intended, update the problem statement to match the template.

issues.description: The visibility of singFarmSongVerse is inconsistent: the UML and the template indicate a private helper method, while the solution implements it as protected. This visibility difference may confuse students about the intended encapsulation and could affect tests or subclassing assumptions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution's singFarmSongVerse to private to match the UML/template, or explicitly document and update the UML/template to use protected if access from subclasses is intended. Aligning visibility removes ambiguity for students.
